newsitem.title: GERMANY: Computer 2000 Q1 sales up, outlook cautious.
newsitem.headline: Computer 2000 Q1 sales up, outlook cautious.

text.p: German computer distributor Computer 2000 AG said on Thursday losses at its U.S. unit dampened its earnings outlook for 1996/97 even as first quarter sales rose 33 percent to 2.1 billion marks ($1.2 billion).

The company, 75 percent owned by diversified German utility Viag AG, said first-quarter earnings in Europe and the Middle East were above target, but Ameriquest Technologies Inc . was still losing money. ($ = 1.687 German Marks)
Computer 2000 Q1 sales up, outlook cautious
Although a turnaround at Ameriquest has not met expectations, chief executive Walter von Szcytnicki said the company expected group sales to grow more than 50 percent over the next three years.

"After 6.64 billion marks in sales in 1995/96 and the revenue development so far this year, we are confident that we can surpass the goal of 10 billion marks in sales for the year 2000," he said at a news conference.
In 1995/96, which ended September 30, Computer 2000 registered a pre-tax profit of 10.1 million marks, but suffered a net loss of 15.6 million marks due to a 52 million marks setback at Ameriquest.
Computer 2000 shares closed floor trading yesterday at 349 marks, up one mark. The shares are up 136 marks from the 52-week low of 213 marks reached on October 8.
